page: Microsoft Azure E48ads_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine from the Eadv6 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 48 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 24 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor operating at 3.7 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The hardware configuration includes 384.0 GB of RAM, providing a 1:8 vCPU-to-memory ratio. Local storage is bundled, consisting of a 2835 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance is Premium Storage capable.

Benchmark data indicates strong performance profiles across multiple domains. The server achieves top 25% results in stress-ng single-core and multi-core tests, alongside high scores in Passmark CPU and memory evaluations. Memory bandwidth for small cached blocks is highly efficient at 3648.86 GB/sec, though large-block uncached read and write operations fall into the average tier. Database operations are a notable strength, with Redis SET operations reaching 67.13 million operations per second and Passmark database operations scoring in the top 25%.

While the instance excels at small-model LLM inference, demonstrating top 10% performance in text generation for a 135M model, it exhibits a clear tradeoff with larger models, dropping to a weak performance tier of 2.59 tokens/sec for 70B model text generation. Given the high memory density, dedicated AMD EPYC cores, and fast local NVMe storage, this server is highly cost-efficient for memory-intensive workloads that do not require discrete GPU acceleration. It is optimally suited for relational databases, in-memory caching layers like Redis, software compilation, and medium-scale data processing tasks.
description: Microsoft Azure E48ads_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor with 48 dedicated vCPUs, 24 physical cores, and a 3.7 GHz clock speed. Built on the x86_64 architecture and managed via Microsoft Hyper-V, it features 384.0 GB of RAM and a bundled 2835 GB local NVMe SSD. Performance benchmarks place this instance in the top 25% for multi-core CPU execution, database operations, and small-block memory bandwidth, with Redis SET operations reaching 67.13 million operations per second. However, a key tradeoff is its weak performance in large-model LLM text generation due to the lack of GPU acceleration. This server is highly suited for memory-intensive workloads, including large databases, in-memory caching, and software compilation.
